body.heading: Midnight, twelve times
paragraphs: In Spain, the year turns to the sound of twelve clock bells — and the race to eat one grape with each strike, for luck in each coming month. It is harder than it sounds, and the laughter when someone falls behind is half the point.

In Italy, lentils land on the New Year table because their coin shape suggests prosperity. In Denmark, people leap off chairs at midnight to jump into the year. In Scotland, first-footing sends the first visitor of the year over the threshold with small gifts meant to bless the house.

body.heading: Borrowing a beginning
paragraphs: Every culture marks the turn of the year with the same two ingredients: something symbolic to eat or carry, and people to share it with. The symbols differ; the hope is identical.
Try adopting one small tradition this year — grapes, lentils, a doorstep visit to a friend — and say where it comes from. Traditions grow by being practised, and they travel by being credited.

description: Twelve grapes at midnight in Spain, lucky lentils in Italy, first-footing in Scotland — the world rings in the year in hopeful, delicious ways.
